question: Does explicitly exposing verified capabilities and failure-stage information reduce unsupported candidate assumptions and improve native execution?
treatment: Historical augmented feedback versus the same feedback plus verified feedback-contract-v2 and current failure-stage table
fixed: Same base prompt, candidate history, model gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning setting, token limit and paired generation settings
Same five diagnostic layouts for development; same runtime, original scoring and1100-step budget for the first controlled comparison
generation_plan: Three candidates per condition, log every request/response, API usage, errors and candidate hash; do not regenerate only failures.
offline_gates: Contract: do not infer lift from nominal Z or object absence alone
Runtime: reject invalid imports/unbounded actions using existing admissions
Error handling: distinguish zero-execution planner rejection from partial-action errors
Account for unavailable remaining-step observations; do not pretend backend-only data is public
native_metrics: Actual evaluation score and full success
First violated contract or stop stage
Number of actions completed before stop
Generation Tokens separate from execution/API-only costs
independent_validation: Only after a fixed repair passes development, freeze selection and evaluate new layouts without further tuning. Report all layouts and failures.
budget: No paid calls made now. Any later generation batch must enforce the user-authorized total cap before launching.
limitations: Contract/lint pass is not robot success.
Do not attribute improvement solely to added text length; a size-matched irrelevant-feedback control can be a separate later ablation.
Manual mechanism fixes and auto-generated candidates must remain separate cohorts.
